# S268 — Planning skips a Grok write row instead of failing at the round

*Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-10. Size S. Status: NOT READY until the owner answers Q1 to Q4 below (no adj record exists for them; `adj check "grok.write"` is `not found`). The spec is written for the recommended answers.

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03 (S72 question, option 1). Grok has no write mode: probes 10-12 in testdata/vendors/grok show dontAsk and acceptEdits both refuse headless writes, and bypassPermissions is ruled out. A Grok implementer row in the matrix is still planned (matrixUse 'used as grok') and then fails when the round runs. Proposed: skip such a row at plan time with a reason, and answer a launch override with bad_params. Depends on S72 landing. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

*Proposed.* The planner keeps every matrix row that has an adapter, so a Grok row in the implementer chain is planned and only fails when the round runs, after a worktree and a run exist.

- `internal/agent/grok/grok.go:61-62`: `Spec.Args` returns "write roles are not supported" for any non-read-only spec. Probes 10 and 11 (`testdata/vendors/grok/10-write-dontask.*`, `11-write-acceptedits.*`) show a headless write refused under `dontAsk` and `acceptEdits`; probe 12 (`12-write-outside.*`) covers a write outside the repo. The owner ruled out `bypassPermissions` and `--always-approve` on 2026-11-03.
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:511` and `:531` add every row whose agent is in `matrixAdapters` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:415`) to the role's chain, whatever the role. `matrixUse` (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:177-190`) then prints `used as grok` for a Grok implementer row, so the matrix view and the plan both promise a run that cannot happen.
- A launch override is checked only with `supportsVendor` (`internal/daemon/runner.go:93`), which accepts `grok` for the implementer.
- Docs already say the failure happens at the round: `docs/guide.md:216-218` ("so a Grok implementer row fails when it runs") and `docs/how-it-works.md:108-109`.
- Only the implementer writes among the roles ork runs. The gate, reviewer, architect, UI pass and spec check use read-only permissions (`internal/engine/perm.go:83-89`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:275`); confirm this against `engine.ResolvePermission` while implementing and key the rule on the resolved `Permission.ReadOnly`, not on a role name, if it is cheap.
- `grok-local` rows (`engine.IsLocalVendor`, `internal/engine/vendors.go:32`) run through the same `grok.Spec` (`internal/daemon/runner.go:168`, `req.Vendor` is the binary), so they hit the same refusal today and are covered by the same rule. S305 lifts the ban for local rows later; this slice puts the rule in one small function so S305 changes one place, and says nothing else about it.

Open owner questions (the owner answers before the relay starts; each is a design choice, none is decided here):
- Q1 what a launch override with a Grok implementer entry gets. (a) `bad_params` naming the vendor and role, same as an unsupported vendor (recommended: the findings propose it, the override is explicit so there is nothing to fall back to, and the error comes before a run exists). (b) skip the entry like a matrix row and plan on with the rest, refusing only when none is left. (c) accept it and let the round fail (today).
- Q2 what happens when every implementer row is a Grok row. (a) refuse planning with `bad_params`-style text that names the skipped rows (recommended: nothing can run, and the existing text "lineup has no row with an adapter for implementer" would mislead because the rows have an adapter). (b) keep the existing message unchanged.
- Q3 wording of the skip reason. (a) `skipped: grok cannot write, so it cannot be the implementer` in the matrix `use` column, and the same text (with the row id) appended to `plan.Note` (recommended: it follows the existing `skipped: ...` form of `launcherMissing`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:419-427`). (b) `not used: grok runs read-only roles only`. (c) another wording from the owner.
- Q4 whether the skipped row shows in the TUI. (a) it shows only where the matrix view and the plan note already print ork's `use` text, with no new TUI element, no golden change and no UI pass (recommended: the smallest change; the TUI already renders `use` and the plan note). (b) add a visible mark in the run lineup or matrix editor, which makes this a UI slice (rule u10, row r14) and needs a design answer.

## Failing tests

- Plan: a matrix whose implementer rows are Claude, Grok, Codex gives an implementer chain of Claude and Codex only; the reviewer and gate chains still keep their Grok row (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`, next to `TestPlanKeepsAGrokAlternateAfterTheRecommendedRow`, which is updated to expect no Grok entry in the implementer chain).
- Plan: the skipped row is named in `plan.Note` with the Q3 text and the row's id.
- Plan: when every implementer row is Grok (cloud or `grok-local`), planning fails with the Q2 text and creates no run record.
- Plan: a launch override whose implementer entry has vendor `grok` or `grok-local` is refused with code `bad_params` (Q1 a); a Grok entry in the reviewer or architect override is still accepted.
- Matrix: `roles.matrix` gives a Grok implementer row `use` equal to the Q3 text, a Grok reviewer row still `used as grok`, and a `grok-local` implementer row the same skip text.
- The engine never receives a Grok implementer request in a planned run (a fake runner records vendors per role).

## Implement

1. Add one predicate in `internal/engine/vendors.go`, for example `CanWrite(vendor string) bool`, false for `grok` and `grok-local` and true otherwise, with a comment citing probes 10-12 and the 2026-11-03 owner ruling. S305 changes only this function.
2. In `planRun`, when building the implementer chain (both loops at `internal/daemon/runs.go:511` and `:531` only matter for the implementer; the UI pass chain is read-only and unchanged), skip a row whose vendor fails the predicate and append the skip reason with the row id to `plan.Note`. Gate, reviewer, architect and UI chains are not touched.
3. If the implementer chain is then empty, return the Q2 error instead of "lineup has no row with an adapter".
4. In the override loop, refuse an implementer entry whose vendor fails the predicate with `badParams`, per Q1.
5. In `matrixUse`, for an implementer row whose adapter fails the predicate, return the Q3 skip text (Spec check and UI rows are unaffected).
6. Update the existing tests named in Files, then add the new ones above test-first.
7. Docs (*proposed*): `docs/design.md:205-214` (a Grok row is skipped for the implementer; the override is refused; `use` can read the skip text, and the `roles.matrix` row at `docs/design.md:114`), `docs/guide.md:216-218` and `docs/how-it-works.md:108-109` (replace "fails when it runs").
8. CHANGELOG.md: add a bullet under `## Unreleased` (*proposed*, S268) as the last step.
